build.//: ONE target emits the three bin bundles AND the baked operations artifact (dist/api.ir.json). The second command runs the freshly built bin's hidden `ir-artifact` subcommand, which extracts the client's built service/api.d.ts (so ^build of policy-core-client is required) and writes the artifact beside the bundles in the SAME dist/. Mirrors entrypoint/backlog's build.

options.command: vite build && node dist/cli.js ir-artifact --out dist/api.ir.json

typecheck-spec.//: Type-checks the SPEC corpus (entrypoint/policy/tsconfig.spec.json). Closes lane-reachability rule 6: a tsconfig.spec.json with no compiling target lets the spec corpus carry type errors no gate can see (nx.json production namedInput excludes it). The ratchet fails on any per-file increase over tools/nx-plugins/build/executors/typecheck-spec/policy.baseline.json or on include narrowing. Wired into test.dependsOn so nx affected -t test runs it.

test.//: Partial override: only dependsOn is added (typecheck-spec, so the spec corpus is type-checked before it runs); the command stays the workspace default (vite.config.ts is .ts here, no .mts override needed).

e2e.//: Real-server lane (docs/decisions/0009-test-lanes-unit-vs-e2e.md). Runs ONLY src/**/*.e2e.ts and src/**/*.e2e.test.ts via vitest.e2e.config.ts: the tier P suites that bind a real loopback socket (http-entry.e2e.test.ts). The unit `test` target excludes those files. Reached by CI (`nx affected -t e2e --parallel=1`), never by the local pre-push hook; not env-gated. Cached on content (`cache:true` + inputs, lane-reachability rule 3); declares no outputs. dependsOn mirrors `test` (the suite loads the entry, which builds the policy package).
